Environmental Studies, Minor
The Environmental Studies Minor examines the relationship between people and their environment, the physical and biological
sciences, and important environmental issues. Students analyze historical and contemporary environmental problems by taking
courses in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. Students might pursue this minor in preparation for a career in
environmental research, education, activism, policy or law, among others. Students take one required course and four elective
courses (at least one mush be from the Sciences and the Humanities and Social Sciences categories)
Requirements
Students minoring in Environmental Studies are required to complete five courses (20 credits), distributed as follows:
Required Courses: 4 Credits
HI 3001 - Introduction to Environmental Studies Credits: 4
Elective courses: Science
Students must take a minimum of one (4 credit) of the following elective courses:
BS 2490 - Environmental Science Credits: 4
BS 3450 - Plant Biology Credits: 4
BS 4470 - Ecology Credits: 4
BS 4474 - Microbial Ecology Credits: 4
BS 4491 - Human Ecology Credits: 4
CP 2300 - Weather Studies Credits: 3
CP 2301 - Weather Studies Lab Credits: 1
CP 2400 - Ocean Studies Credits: 3
CP 2401 - Ocean Studies Lab Credits: 1
CP 2500 - Climate Studies Credits: 3
CP 2501 - Climate Studies Lab Credits: 1
CP 2600 - Environmental Analysis of Long Island Credits: 4
